questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristics of the National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs) of India?

options.text: The state government will provide power connectivity, water and other infrastructural facilities.
At least 30% of the total land area proposed for the NIMZ is to be utilized for manufacturing units.
A special purpose vehicle will be constituted to take care of the functioning of NIMZs
It prescribes a minimum area of 10000 hectares for establishing NIMZs.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It prescribes a minimum area of 10000 hectares for establishing NIMZs**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• NIMZs are developed to promote manufacturing and attract investment in the industrial sector, as part of the** National Manufacturing Policy, 2011.**
 
• Each NIMZ is a large industrial cluster, spread over a minimum of **5,000 hectares, with integrated infrastructure,** including **roads, water, and power supply.**
 
• NIMZs aim to increase the share of manufacturing in** India's GDP and generate large-scale employment** in the sector.
 
• Industries in NIMZs receive special incentives, such as** tax benefits, single-window** clearances, and easier compliance with labor laws.
 
• Some of the approved NIMZs are located in** Prakasam (Andhra Pradesh), Medak (Telangana), Aurangabad (Maharashtra), and Dholera (Gujarat).**

questions.question: Rotating Savings and Credit Association (ROSCA) was introduced by Shirley Ardener in the year ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1964**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rotating Savings and Credit Association (ROSCA)** was introduced by Shirley Ardener in the year **1964**.
 
• ROSCA is a group of individuals who come together to save and borrow collectively from a common fund.
 
• Each member of the group contributes a fixed amount to the fund at regular intervals, and one member gets the entire sum collected at each interval.
 
• This process continues until all members have received the sum once.
 
• ROSCA is a traditional form of savings and credit, widely practiced in various parts of the world, particularly in developing countries.
 
• It provides an alternative to formal banking systems, particularly for individuals who may not have access to traditional financial services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shirley Ardener** is an anthropologist and researcher who has extensively studied and documented ROSCAs.
 
• ROSCAs are known by various names in different cultures, such as "tandas" in Latin America, "susus" in West Africa, and "chit funds" in India.
 
• They play a crucial role in financial inclusion by providing a mechanism for saving and accessing credit outside of formal financial institutions.
 
• ROSCAs can also foster a sense of community and mutual support among members.
 
• Despite their benefits, ROSCAs also carry risks, such as the potential for members to default on their contributions.

questions.question: Name the campaign launched by the Madhya Pradesh government on the occasion of National Girl Child Day on January 24, 2021, under the 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' scheme.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PANKH Abhiyan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Pankh campaign,** launched on **National Girl Child Day** on January 24, 2021, is part of the "Beti Bachao Beti Padhao" Scheme administered by the Madhya Pradesh Government and spearheaded by Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
 
• PANKH stands for Protection, Awareness of rights, Nutrition, Knowledge, and Health, encapsulating the key pillars essential for the holistic development of girls.
 
• This initiative is dedicated to fostering the overall growth and well-being of the girl child.
 
• Additionally, the Ladli Laxmi Yojana in Madhya Pradesh represents another noteworthy effort aimed at supporting the welfare of girls in the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Manjhi Kanya Bhagyashree scheme **was introduced in 2015 by the Women and Child Development Department of Maharashtra. It aims to support the welfare and development of girls in the state.
 
• **Udaan** is a project initiated by the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) under the auspices of the Ministry of Human Resource Development, Government of India. 
 
• **The Balika Samriddhi Yojana** is a government program designed to promote the well-being of girls. It provides financial assistance after the birth of a girl child and upon completion of her education, with the objective of combating negative attitudes towards daughters.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true with respect to MRTP Act?

i) The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act (MRTP Act) was repealed and replaced by the Competition Act, 2002.

ii) The asset limit for MRTP companies was fixed at Rs. 25 crores by the first/original Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act (MRTP Act).

iii) The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act (MRTP Act) was first passed in 1969.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only i and iii**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• i) **True**: The MRTP Act was indeed repealed and replaced by the Competition Act, 2002, which aimed to promote and sustain competition in the markets.
 
• ii) **False**: The original asset limit for MRTP companies **was set at Rs. 20 crores, not Rs. 25 crores.**
 
• iii)**True**: The MRTP Act was enacted in 1969 to prevent monopolistic and restrictive trade practices.
 
• Thus, **statements i and iii are true** with respect to the MRTP Act.

questions.question: Which of the following is the compelling factor that produced a very high repayment rate of 98% in the concept of lending to groups of poor women, initiated by Dr Yunus?

options.text: Removal of the defaulter from the group
Joint liability putting social pressure to repay loans
Use of the services of aggressive loan recovery agents

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Joint liability putting social pressure to repay loans.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Joint liability:-**

 
 
• It means that all members of a group are responsible for each other's loans.
 
• Therefore, if one member defaults on a loan, the other members are responsible for repaying it. This puts social pressure on the group to repay loans on time.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the concept of lending to groups of poor women, initiated by Dr Yunus, joint liability was used as a compelling factor to ensure a high repayment rate.
 
• The removal of a defaulter from the group may seem like a viable solution, but it does not address the root cause of defaulting on loans. Moreover, it may lead to social ostracization of the defaulter, which is not desirable.
 
• Involvement of 'loan sharks' and the use of the services of aggressive loan recovery agents (option 4) are illegal and unethical means of recovering loans. They do not address the root cause of defaulting on loans and may lead to further indebtedness of borrowers.

questions.question: When was the Direct Tax Code Bill introduced in the Parliament of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2010.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **12 August 2009**, the first draft of the **Direct Tax Code Bill **was created.
 
• **In 2010, a Revised Discussion Paper was created.**
 
• **In 2010, The Direct Tax Code bill was introduced in Parliament,** and a Standing Committee of Finance (SCF) was appointed for a detailed discussion.
 
• In 2012, the committee submitted its report to Parliament.
 
• In 2014, a revised version of the Direct Tax Code was created after the committee report.
 
• The bill lapsed due to the change in government after the general elections.
 
• **In 2017**, An expert committee was set up to draft a fresh Direct Tax Code.
 
• In Aug 2019, the task force report was submitted to the Finance Minister.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Tax Type
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Income Tax
 A tax on the income earned by individuals, HUFs, companies, and other entities.
 
 

 Goods and Services Tax (GST)
 A value-added tax on the supply of goods and services, which replaced several indirect taxes such as excise duty, VAT, and service tax.
 
 

 Corporate Tax
 A tax on the profits earned by companies and other business entities.
 
 

 Capital Gains Tax
 A tax on the profits earned from the sale of capital assets such as property, shares, and mutual funds.
 
 

 Wealth Tax
 A tax on the net wealth of individuals and HUFs, which was abolished in 2015.
 
 

 Customs Duty
 A tax on the import and export of goods across India's borders.
 
 

 Excise Duty
 A tax on the production and manufacture of goods within the country.
 
 

 Securities Transaction Tax (STT)
 A tax on the purchase and sale of securities such as stocks, bonds, and mutual funds.
 
 

 Professional Tax
 A tax on the income earned by professionals such as doctors, lawyers, and chartered accountants.
 
 

 Property Tax
 A tax on the ownership or occupation of property, which is levied by local authorities such as municipalities and panchayats.

questions.question: How many districts of Uttar Pradesh started the second phase of Mission Indradhanush 2.0 at the block level on 7 January 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**​35**__.

__

• The aim of the program launched by the central government in 2017 is to achieve 90% vaccination coverage in children of less than 2 years in the state.
 
• Under the program, around** 66 thousand sessions will be organized for vaccination of more than 5.5 lakh children.**
 
• Salient features:
 __
 
• Four rounds of activity will be conducted over 7 working days excluding holidays.
 
• Enhanced focus will be on the left-outs.
 
• Focus on the Urban and underserved tribal population will be laid.
 
• Interministerial coordination.
 
• Enhanced immunisation sessions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​**Mission Indradhanush:**

 
 
• It was launched in 2014 by the union government after realising the incompetence of the Universal Immunisation Programme which could achieve 65% immunisation only.
 
• This mission was launched to achieve full immunisation for the children up to 2 years of age and all pregnant ladies.
 
• 201 districts were identified in 28 states under this mission.
 
 
 
• Intensifie**d Mission Indradhanush:**
 
 
• It was launched in October 2017 to reach out to all the children and Pregnant ladies who were left under Mission Indradhanush.
 
• This programme aimed to ensure full vaccination of more than 90% of the target population.
 
• It was also conducted in 4 rounds in 173 focus districts.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is NOT correct with respect to the poverty line?

I. In India, it is normally estimated after every ten years.

II. The proportion of people below the poverty line is not the same for all social groups and economic categories in India.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Only I**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**

__
 
• Poverty means that the income level from employment is so low that basic human needs can't be met.
 
• The poverty line varies with time and place.
 
• A poor household is defined as one with an expenditure level below a specific poverty line.
 
• As per the Rangarajan committee report (2014), the poverty line is estimated as a Monthly Per Capita Expenditure of Rs. 1407 in urban areas and Rs. 972 in rural areas.
 
• A common method used to measure poverty is based on income.
 
• Poverty line estimation in India is based on consumption expenditure and not on income levels.
 
• Poverty is measured based on consumer expenditure surveys by the National Sample Survey Organisation.
 
• The incidence of poverty is measured by the poverty ratio, which is the ratio of the number of poor to the total population expressed as a percentage. It is also known as the head-count ratio.
 
• Alagh Committee (1979) determined a poverty line based on a minimum daily requirement of 2400 and 2100 calories for an adult in Rural and Urban areas respectively.
 
• The measurement limits of the poverty line may be based on the consumption levels of the population.
 
• **The poverty line in India is not calculated on a regular ten-year basis. Instead, it is periodically updated by the Government of India.** ***Statement I is Incorrect.**__*
 
• The poverty line is defined as the minimum level of income or consumption necessary to meet basic needs and lead a decent life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information:__**

 
• In 2011, the Suresh Tendulkar Committee defined the poverty line on the basis of monthly spending on food, education, health, electricity and transport.
 
• According to this estimate, a person who spends Rs. 27.2 in rural areas and Rs. 33.3 in urban areas a day are defined as living below the poverty line. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e08a7aae8e89c4f361bd9dd29a2cef59abd13318299c387bae751529b5d0c59.png]
